The audit gate that could not run

PR playground for #4023, closing #4015.

tests/security/test-npm-audit.sh audits all six tracked lockfiles and is run by tests/security/run-security-tests.sh. Its retry wrapper called GNU timeout unconditionally. That binary ships on the CI runners and not on a stock macOS, so the shell exited 127 before npm ever started, and the gate attributed the empty result to the registry rather than to the missing binary. It failed closed, six for six, which is the right direction but the wrong sentence: nobody reading it would go looking for coreutils. This PR resolves timeout, then gtimeout, then falls back to a bash watchdog that reports GNU's exit 124, and it retires audit allowlist entry 1124006, which expired on 2026-09-01 and no longer applies now that @hono/node-server is 2.1.0.

Before, on macOS

  x root: npm audit produced no usable JSON report
      npm-audit-with-retry.sh: line 58: timeout: command not found
  ...
  Total: 6  |  Passed: 0  |  Failed: 6

After

  v root: 0 findings >= moderate
  v docs/site: 0 findings >= moderate
  v src/hooks: 0 findings >= moderate
  v src/mcp-server: 0 findings >= moderate
  v orchestkit-demos: 0 findings >= moderate
  v hook-contract/examples/generic-client: 0 findings >= moderate
  Total: 6  |  Passed: 6  |  Failed: 0

Why no test caught it

  • tests/ci/test-npm-audit-with-retry.sh put a fake timeout on PATH in every case, so the unconditional call was invisible to the one test written to cover it.
  • Two cases now run with a PATH carrying neither timeout nor gtimeout, plus a positive control asserting the isolated PATH really removed both, so they cannot decay back into re-testing the shimmed path.

Reproduce it

bash tests/ci/test-npm-audit-with-retry.sh
bash tests/security/test-npm-audit.sh
The five advisories named in #4015 were already gone at HEAD: PR #4014 moved hono to 4.13.7 and the generic-client lock to vitest 4.1.11. No bump was made here and no audit level was lowered.
